¶ Mordecai went out robed in royal apparel, wearing a golden crown and a diadem of fine purple linen. The people in Susa saw it and rejoiced.
The Jews had light and gladness
in every city and province where the ordinance was published. Wherever the proclamation took place, the Jews had joy and gladness, feasting and mirth. Many of the Gentiles were circumcised and became Jews for fear of the Jews.
























¶ Now in the twelfth month, on the thirteenth day of the month, which is Adar, the letters written by the king arrived.
In that day, the adversaries of the Jews perished; for no one resisted, through fear of them.
Because the chiefs of the local governors, and the princes and the royal scribes, honoured the Jews; for the fear of Mordecai was upon them.
Because the order of the king was in force, that he should be celebrated in all the kingdom.

¶ Then the king said to Esther, “The Jews have slain five hundred men in the city Susa. What do you think they have done in the rest of the country? What more do you ask, that it may be done for you?”
¶ Esther said to the king, “Let it be granted to the Jews to do the same to them tomorrow. Also, hang the bodies of the ten sons of Haman.”
¶ He permitted it to be done; and he gave up to the Jews of the city the bodies of the sons of Haman to hang.
The Jews assembled in Susa on the fourteenth day of Adar and killed three hundred men, but plundered no property.
¶ The rest of the Jews who were in the kingdom assembled, and helped one another, and obtained rest from their enemies; for they destroyed fifteen thousand of them on the thirteenth day of Adar, but took no spoil.
They rested on the fourteenth of the same month, and kept it as a day of rest with joy and gladness.
¶ The Jews in the city of Susa assembled also on the fourteenth day and rested; and they also observed the fifteenth with joy and gladness.
On this account then, the Jews dispersed in every foreign land keep the fourteenth of Adar as a\f + \fr 9:19 \fl Greek \ft good day.\f* holy day with joy, each sending gifts of food to his neighbour.
¶ Mordecai wrote these things in a book and sent them to the Jews, as many as were in the kingdom of Ahasuerus, both those who were near and those who were far away,
to establish these as joyful days and to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar;
for on these days the Jews obtained rest from their enemies; and in that month, which was Adar, in which a change was made for them from mourning to joy, and from sorrow to a holiday, to spend the whole of it in good days of\f + \fr 9:22 \fl Greek \ft weddings.\f* feasting and gladness, sending portions to their friends and to the poor.
And the Jews consented to this as Mordecai wrote to them,
showing how Haman the son of Hammedatha the Macedonian fought against them, how he made a decree and threw\f + \fr 9:24 \fl Greek \ft lot.\f* lots to destroy them utterly;
also how he went in to the king, telling him to hang Mordecai; but all the calamities he tried to bring upon the Jews came upon himself, and he was hanged, along with his children.
Therefore these days were called Purim, because of the lots (for in their language they are called Purim) because of the words of this letter, and because of all they suffered on this account, and all that happened to them.
Mordecai established it, and the Jews took upon themselves, upon their offspring, and upon those who were joined to them to observe it, neither would they on any account behave differently; but these days were to be a memorial kept in every generation, city, family, and province.
These days of Purim shall be kept forever, and their memorial shall not fail in any generation.
¶ Queen Esther the daughter of Aminadab and Mordecai the Jew wrote all that they had done, and gave the confirmation of the letter about Purim.
Mordecai and Esther the queen established this decision on their own, pledging their own well-being to their plan.
And Esther established it by a command forever, and it was written for a memorial.
¶ The king levied a tax upon his kingdom both by land and sea.

₁ When I come into my house, I will find rest with her.₂ Because conversation with her has no bitterness,₂ and living with her has no pain, but gladness and joy.
₁ When I considered these things in myself,₂ and thought in my heart how immortality is in kinship to wisdom,
₁ and in her friendship is good delight,₂ and in the labours of her hands is wealth that doesn’t fail,₂ and understanding is in her companionship,₂ and great renown in having fellowship with her words,₂ I went about seeking how to take her to myself.
₁ Now I was a clever child, and received a good soul.
₂ Or rather, being good, I came into an undefiled body.
₁ But perceiving that I could not otherwise possess wisdom unless God gave her to me—₂ yes, and to know and understand by whom the grace is given—₂ I pleaded with the master and implored him, and with my whole heart I said:
₁ “O God of my ancestors and master of mercy,₂ who made all things by your word;
₁ and by your wisdom you formed man,₂ that he should have dominion over the creatures that were made by you,
₁ and rule the world in holiness and righteousness,₂ and execute judgement in uprightness of soul,
₂ give me wisdom, her who sits by you on your thrones.₁ Don’t reject me from amongst your\f + \fr 9:4 \ft Or, \fqa children\f* servants,
₂ because I am your servant and the son of your handmaid,₂ a weak and short-lived man,₂ with little power to understand judgement and laws.
₁ Because even if a man is perfect amongst the sons of men,₂ if the wisdom that comes from you is not with him, he will count for nothing.
₁ You chose me to be king of your people,₂ and a judge for your sons and daughters.
₁ You gave a command to build a sanctuary on your holy mountain,₂ and\f + \fr 9:8 \ft Or, \fqa a place of sacrifice\f* an altar in the city where you live,₂ a copy of the holy tent which you prepared from the beginning.
₁ Wisdom is with you and knows your works,₂ and was present when you were making the world,₂ and understands what is pleasing in your eyes,₂ and what is right according to your commandments.
₁ Send her from the holy heavens,₂ and ask her to come from the throne of your glory,₂ that being present with me she may work,₂ and I may learn what pleases you well.
₁ Because she knows all things and understands,₂ and she will guide me prudently in my actions.₂ She will guard me in her glory.
₁ So my works will be acceptable.₂ I will judge your people righteously,₂ and I will be worthy of my father’s\f + \fr 9:12 \ft Gr. \fqa thrones.\f* throne.
₁ Because what man will know the counsel of God?₂ Or who will conceive what the master wills?
₁ Because the thoughts of mortals are unstable,₂ and our plans are prone to fail.
₁ Because a corruptible body weighs down the soul.₂ The earthy tent burdens a mind that is full of cares.
₁ We can hardly guess the things that are on earth,₂ and we find the things that are close at hand with labour;₂ but who has traced out the things that are in the heavens?
₁ Who gained knowledge of your counsel, unless you gave wisdom,₂ and sent your holy spirit from on high?
₁ It was thus that the ways of those who are on earth were corrected,₂ and men were taught the things that are pleasing to you.₂ They were saved through wisdom.”
₁ Wisdom\f + \fr 10:1 \ft Gr. \fqa She.\f* guarded to the end the first formed father of the world, who was created alone,₂ and delivered him out of his own transgression,

₁ But when an unrighteous man fell away from her in his anger,₂ he perished himself in the rage with which he killed his brother.

₁ When a righteous man was a fugitive from a brother’s wrath,\f + \fr 10:10 \ft Gr. \fqa she.\f* wisdom guided him in straight paths.₂ She showed him God’s kingdom, and gave him knowledge of holy things.₂ She prospered him in his toils, and multiplied the fruits of his labour.
₁ When in their covetousness men dealt harshly with him,₂ she stood by him and made him rich.
₁ She guarded him from enemies,₂ and she kept him safe from those who lay in wait.₂ Over his severe conflict, she watched as judge,₂ that he might know that godliness is more powerful than every one.
₁ When a righteous man was sold,\f + \fr 10:13 \ft Gr. \fqa she.\f* wisdom didn’t forsake him,₂ but she delivered him from sin.₂ She went down with him into a dungeon,

₁ Wisdom\f + \fr 10:15 \ft Gr. \fqa she.\f* delivered a holy people and a blameless seed from a nation of oppressors.
₁ She entered into the soul of a servant of the master,₂ and withstood terrible kings in wonders and signs.
₁ She rendered to holy men a reward of their toils.₂ She guided them along a marvellous way,₂ and became to them a covering in the day-time,₂ and a starry flame through the night.
₁ She brought them over the Red sea,₂ and led them through much water;
₁ but she drowned their enemies,₂ and she threw them up from the bottom of the deep.
₁ Therefore the righteous plundered the ungodly,₂ and they sang praise to your holy name, O master,₂ and extolled with one accord your hand that fought for them,
₁ because wisdom opened the mouth of the mute,₁ and made the tongues of babes to speak clearly.
₁ Wisdom prospered their works in the hand of a holy prophet.
₁ They travelled through a desert without inhabitant,₂ and they pitched their tents in trackless regions.
₁ They withstood enemies and repelled foes.
₁ They thirsted, and they called upon you,₂ and water was given to them out of the\f + \fr 11:4 \ft See Deuteronomy 8:15; Psalms 114:8.\f* flinty rock,₂ and healing of their thirst out of the hard stone.
₁ Because by what things their foes were punished,₂ by these they in their need were benefitted.
₁ When enemies were troubled with clotted blood₂ instead of a river’s ever-flowing fountain,

₁ having shown by the thirst which they had suffered₂ how you punished the adversaries.
₁ Because when they were tried, although chastened in mercy,₂ they learnt how the ungodly were tormented, being judged with wrath.
₁ Because you tested these as a father admonishing them;₂ but you searched out those as a stern king condemning them.
₁ Yes and whether they were far off or near,₂ they were equally distressed;
₁ for a double grief seized them,₂ and a groaning at the memory of things past.
₁ Because when they heard that through their own punishments the others benefitted,₂ they recognised the master.
₁ Because him who long before was thrown out and exposed they stopped mocking.₂ In the end of what happened, they marvelled,₂ having thirsted in another manner than the righteous.
₁ But in return for the senseless imaginings of their unrighteousness,₂ wherein they were led astray to worship irrational reptiles and wretched vermin,₂ you sent upon them a multitude of irrational creatures to punish them,
₂ that they might learn that by what things a man sins, by these he is punished.
₁ Because your all-powerful hand₂ that created the world out of formless matter₂ didn’t lack means to send upon them a multitude of bears, fierce lions,
₂ or newly-created and unknown wild animals, full of rage,₂ either breathing out a blast of fiery breath,₂ or belching out smoke,₂ or flashing dreadful sparks from their eyes;
₁ which had power not only to consume them by their violence,₂ but to destroy them even by the terror of their sight.
₁ Yes and without these they might have fallen by a single breath,₂ being pursued by Justice, and scattered abroad by the breath of your power;₂ but you arranged all things by measure, number, and weight.
₁ Because to be greatly strong is yours at all times.₂ Who could withstand the might of your arm?
₁ Because the whole world before you is as a grain in a balance,₂ and as a drop of dew that comes down upon the earth in the morning.
₁ But you have mercy on all men, because you have power to do all things,₂ and you overlook the sins of men to the end that they may repent.
₁ Because you love all things that are,₂ and abhor none of the things which you made;₂ Because you never would have formed anything if you hated it.
₁ How would anything have endured unless you had willed it?₂ Or that which was not called by you, how would it have been preserved?
₁ But you spare all things, because they are yours,₂ O Sovereign master, you who love the living.
₁ Because your incorruptible spirit is in all things.
₁ Therefore you convict little by little those who fall from the right way,₂ and, putting them in remembrance by the things wherein they sin, you admonish them,₂ that escaping from their wickedness they may believe in you, O master.
₁ Because truly the old inhabitants of your holy land,
₂ hating them because they practised detestable works of enchantments and unholy rites—

₁ Because they were a cursed seed from the beginning.₂ It wasn’t through fear of any that you left them unpunished for their sins.

₁ No king or prince will be able to confront you₂ about those whom you have punished.

₁ Because your strength is the source of righteousness,₂ and your sovereignty over all makes you to forbear all.

₁ Therefore also the unrighteous that lived in a life of folly,₂ you tormented through their own abominations.
₁ Because truly they went astray very far in the ways of error,₂ Taking as gods those animals\f + \fr 12:24 \ft Gr. \fqa living creatures: \ft and so elsewhere in this book.\f* which even amongst their enemies were held in dishonour,₂ deceived like foolish babes.

₁ Because truly all men who had no perception of God were foolish by nature,₂ and didn’t gain power to know him who exists from the good things that are seen.₂ They didn’t recognise the architect from his works.
₁ But they thought that either fire, or wind, or swift air,₂ or circling stars, or raging water, or luminaries of heaven₂ were gods that rule the world.
₁ If it was through delight in their beauty that they took them to be gods,₂ let them know how much better their Sovereign master is than these,₂ for the first author of beauty created them.
₁ But if it was through astonishment at their power and influence,₂ then let them understand from them how much more powerful he who formed them is.
₁ Because from the greatness of the beauty of created things,₂ mankind forms the corresponding perception of their Maker.\f + \fr 13:5 \ft Gr. \fqa is the first maker of them seen.\f*
₁ But yet for these men there is but small blame,₂ for they too perhaps go astray₂ while they are seeking God and desiring to find him.

₁ But again even they are not to be excused.
₁ Because if they had power to know so much,₂ that they should be able to explore the world,₂ how is it that they didn’t find the Sovereign master sooner?
₁ But they were miserable, and their hopes were in dead things,₂ who called them gods which are works of men’s hands,₂ gold and silver, skilfully made, and likenesses of animals,₂ or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.
₁ Yes and some\f + \fr 13:11 \ft Gr. \fqa carpenter who is a woodcutter.\f* woodcutter might saw down a tree that is easily moved,₂ skilfully strip away all its bark,₂ and fashion it in attractive form, make a useful vessel to serve his life’s needs.

₁ Because neither did the dark recesses that held them guard them from fears,₂ but terrifying sounds rang around them,₂ and dismal phantoms appeared with unsmiling faces.
₁ And no power of fire prevailed to give light,₂ neither were the brightest flames of the stars strong enough to illuminate that gloomy night;
₁ but only the glimmering of a self-kindled fire appeared to them, full of fear.₂ In terror, they considered the things which they saw₂ to be worse than that sight, on which they could not gaze.
₁ The mockeries of their magic arts were powerless, now,₂ and a shameful rebuke of their boasted understanding:
₁ Because those who promised to drive away terrors and disorders from a sick soul,₂ these were sick with a ludicrous fearfulness.
₁ Because even if no troubling thing frighted them,₂ yet, scared with the creeping of vermin and hissing of serpents,
₁ they perished trembling in fear,₂ refusing even to look at the air, which could not be escaped on any side.
₁ Because wickedness, condemned by a witness within, is a coward thing,₂ and, being pressed hard by conscience, always has added forecasts of the worst.
₂ Because fear is nothing else but a surrender of the help which reason offers;
₂ and from within, the expectation of being less₂ prefers ignorance of the cause that brings the torment.
₁ But they, all through the night which was powerless indeed,₂ and which came upon them out of the recesses of powerless Hades,₂ sleeping the same sleep,
₂ now were haunted by monstrous apparitions,₂ and now were paralysed by their soul’s surrendering;₂ for sudden and unexpected fear came upon them.
₁ So then whoever it might be, sinking down in his place,₂ was kept captive, shut up in that prison which was not barred with iron;
₁ for whether he was a farmer, or a shepherd,₂ or a labourer whose toils were in the wilderness,₂ he was overtaken, and endured that inescapable sentence;₂ for they were all bound with one chain of darkness.
₁ Whether there was a whistling wind,₂ or a melodious sound of birds amongst the spreading branches,₂ or a measured fall of water running violently,
₂ or a harsh crashing of rocks hurled down,₂ or the swift course of animals bounding along unseen,₂ or the voice of wild animals harshly roaring,₂ or an echo rebounding from the hollows of the mountains,₂ all these things paralysed them with terror.
₁ Because the whole world was illuminated with clear light,₂ and was occupied with unhindered works,
₁ But for your holy ones there was great light.₂ Their enemies, hearing their voice but not seeing their form,₂ counted it a happy thing that they too had suffered,
₁ yet for that they do not hurt them, though wronged by them before, they are thankful;₂ and because they had been at variance with them, they begged for pardon.
₁ Therefore you provided a burning pillar of fire,₂ to be a guide for your people’s unknown journey,₂ and a harmless sun for their glorious exile.
₁ Because the Egyptians well deserved to be deprived of light and imprisoned by darkness,₂ they who had imprisoned your children,₂ through whom the incorruptible light of the law was to be given to the race of men.
₁ After they had taken counsel to kill the babes of the holy ones,₂ and when a single child had been abandoned and saved to convict them of their sin,₂ you took away from them their multitude of children,₂ and destroyed all their army together in a mighty flood.
₁ Our fathers were made aware of that night beforehand,₂ that, having sure knowledge, they might be cheered by the oaths which they had trusted.
₁ Salvation of the righteous and destruction of the enemies was expected by your people.
₁ Because as you took vengeance on the adversaries,₂ by the same means, calling us to yourself, you glorified us.
₁ Because holy children of good men offered sacrifice in secret,₂ and with one consent they agreed to the covenant of the divine law,₂ that they would partake alike in the same good things and the same perils,₂ the fathers already leading the sacred songs of praise.
₁ But the discordant cry of the enemies echoed back,₂ and a pitiful voice of lamentation for children was spread abroad.
₁ Both servant and master were punished with the same just doom,₂ and the commoner suffering the same as king;
₁ Yes, they all together, under one form of death,₂ had corpses without number.₁ Because the living were not sufficient even to bury them,₂ Since at a single stroke, their most cherished offspring was consumed.
₁ Because while they were disbelieving all things by reason of the enchantments,₂ upon the destruction of the firstborn they confessed the people to be God’s children.
₁ Because while peaceful silence wrapped all things,₂ and night in her own swiftness was half spent,
₁ your all-powerful word leapt from heaven, from the royal throne,₂ a stern warrior, into the midst of the doomed land,
₁ bearing as a sharp sword your authentic commandment,₂ and standing, it filled all things with death,₂ and while it touched the heaven it stood upon the earth.
₁ Then immediately apparitions in dreams terribly troubled them,₂ and unexpected fears came upon them.
₁ And each, one thrown here half dead, another there,₂ made known why he was dying;
₁ for the dreams, disturbing them, forewarned them of this,₂ that they might not perish without knowing why they were afflicted.
₁ The experience of death also touched the righteous,₂ and a multitude were destroyed in the wilderness,₂ but the wrath didn’t last long.
₁ Because a blameless man hurried to be their champion,₂ bringing the weapon of his own ministry,₂ prayer, and the atoning sacrifice of incense.₁ He withstood the indignation and set an end to the calamity,₂ showing that he was your servant.
₁ And he overcame the anger,₂ not by strength of body, not by force of weapons,₂ but by his word, he subdued the avenger₂ by bringing to remembrance oaths and covenants made with the fathers.
₁ Because when the dead had already fallen in heaps one upon another,₂ he intervened and stopped the wrath,₂ and cut off its way to the living.
₁ Because the whole world was pictured on his long robe,₂ and the glories of the fathers were upon the engraving of the four rows of precious stones,₂ and your majesty was upon the diadem on his head.
₁ The destroyer yielded to these, and they feared;₂ for it was enough only to test the wrath.
₁ But indignation without mercy came upon the ungodly to the end;₂ for God also foreknew their future,
₁ how, having changed their minds to let your people go,₂ and having sped them eagerly on their way,₂ they would change their minds and pursue them.
₁ Because while they were yet in the midst of their mourning,₂ and lamenting at the graves of the dead,₂ they made another foolish decision,₂ and pursued as fugitives those whom they had begged to leave and driven out.
₁ Because the doom which they deserved was drawing them to this end,₂ and it made them forget the things that had happened to them,₂ that they might fill up the punishment which was yet lacking from their torments,
₂ and that your people might journey on by a marvellous road,₂ but they themselves might find a strange death.
₁ Because the whole creation, each part in its diverse kind, was made new again,₂ complying with your commandments,₂ that your servants might be kept unharmed.
₁ Then the cloud that overshadowed the camp was seen,₂ and dry land rising up out of what had been water,₂ out of the Red sea an unhindered highway,₂ and a grassy plain out of the violent surge,
₂ by which they passed over with all their army,₂ these who were covered with your hand,₂ having seen strange marvels.
₁ Because like horses they roamed at large,₂ and they skipped about like lambs,₂ praising you, O master, who was their deliverer.
₁ Because they still remembered the things that happened in the time of their sojourning,₂ how instead of bearing cattle, the land brought forth lice,₂ and instead of fish, the river spewed out a multitude of frogs.
₁ But afterwards, they also saw a new kind of birds,₂ when, led on by desire, they asked for luxurious dainties;
₁ for, to comfort them, quails came up for them from the sea.
₁ Punishments came upon the sinners,₂ not without the signs that were given beforehand by the violence of the thunder,₂ for they justly suffered through their own wickednesses,₂ for the hatred which they practised towards guests was grievous indeed.
₁ Because while the others didn’t receive the strangers when they came to them,₂ the Egyptians made slaves of guests who were their benefactors.
₁ And not only so, but while punishment of some sort will come upon the former,₂ since they received as enemies those who were aliens;
₂ because these first welcomed with feastings,₂ and then afflicted with dreadful toils,₂ those who had already shared with them in the same rights.
₁ And moreover they were stricken with loss of sight₂ (even as were those others at the righteous man’s doors),₂ when, being surrounded with yawning darkness,₂ they each looked for the passage through his own door.
₁ Because as the notes of a lute vary the character of the rhythm,₂ even so the elements, changing their order one with another,₂ continuing always in its sound,₂ as may clearly be conjectured from the sight of the things that have happened.
₁ Because creatures of the dry land were turned into creatures of the waters,₂ and creatures that swim moved upon the land.
₁ Fire kept the mastery of its own power in water,₂ and water forgot its quenching nature.
₁ On the contrary, flames didn’t consume flesh of perishable creatures that walked amongst them,₂ neither did they melt the crystalline grains of ambrosial food that were melted easily.
₁ Because in all things, O master, you magnified your people,₂ and you glorified them and didn’t lightly regard them,₂ standing by their side in every time and place.
₁ All wisdom comes from the master,₂ and is with him forever.

₁ A modest woman is grace upon grace.₂ There are no scales that can weigh the value of a self-controlled soul.

₁ Because two things my heart is grieved,₂ and for the third anger comes upon me:₂ a warrior who suffers for poverty,₂ men of understanding who are counted as garbage,₂ and one who turns back from righteousness to sin—₂ the master will prepare him for the sword!
₁ It is difficult for a merchant to keep himself from wrong doing,₂ and for a retailer to be acquitted of sin.
₁ Many have sinned for profit.₂ He who seeks to multiply wealth will turn his eye away.
₁ As a nail will stick fast between the joinings of stones,₂ so sin will thrust itself in between buying and selling.
₁ Unless a person holds on diligently to the fear of the master,₂ his house will be overthrown quickly.
₁ In the shaking of a sieve, the refuse remains,₂ so does the filth of man in his thoughts.
₁ The furnace tests the potter’s vessels;₂ so the test of a person is in his thoughts.
₁ The fruit of a tree discloses its cultivation,₂ so is the utterance of the thought of a person’s heart.
₁ Praise no man before you hear his thoughts,₂ for this is how people are tested.
₁ If you follow righteousness, you will obtain it,₁ and put it on like a long robe of glory.
₁ Birds will return to their own kind,₂ so truth will return to those who practise it.
₁ The lion lies in wait for prey.₂ So does sin for those who do evil.
₁ The discourse of a godly man is always wise,₂ but the fool changes like the moon.
₁ Limit your time amongst people void of understanding,₂ but persevere amongst the thoughtful.
₁ The talk of fools is offensive.₂ Their laughter is wantonly sinful.
₁ Their talk with much swearing makes hair stand upright.₂ Their strife makes others plug their ears.
₁ The strife of the proud leads to bloodshed.₂ Their abuse of each other is a grievous thing to hear.
₁ He who reveals secrets destroys trust,₂ and will not find a close friend.
₁ Love a friend, and keep faith with him;₂ but if you reveal his secrets,₂ you shall not follow him;
₁ for as a man has destroyed his enemy,₂ so you have destroyed the friendship of your neighbour.
₁ As a bird which you have released out of your hand,₂ so you have let your neighbour go, and you will not catch him again.
₁ Don’t pursue him, for he has gone far away,₂ and has escaped like a gazelle out of the snare.
₁ Because a wound may be bound up, and after abuse there may be reconciliation;₂ but he who reveals secrets is without hope.
₁ One who winks the eye contrives evil things;₂ and those who know him will keep their distance.
₁ When you are present, he will speak sweetly,₂ and will admire your words;₂ but afterward he will twist his speech₂ and set a trap in your words.
₁ I have hated many things, but nothing like him.₂ The master will hate him.
₁ One who casts a stone straight up casts it on his own head.₂ A deceitful blow opens wounds.
₁ He who digs a pit will fall into it.₂ He who sets a snare will be caught in it.
₁ He who does evil things, they will roll back upon him,₂ and he will not know where they came from.
₁ Mockery and reproach are from the arrogant.₂ Vengeance lies in wait for them like a lion.
₁ Those who rejoice at the fall of the godly will be caught in a snare.₂ Anguish will consume them before they die.
₁ Wrath and anger, these also are abominations.₂ A sinner will possess them.
₁ He who takes vengeance will find vengeance from the master,₂ and he will surely make his sins firm.
₁ Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done,₂ and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.
₁ Does anyone harbour anger against another₂ and expect healing from the master?
₁ Upon a man like himself he has no mercy,₂ and does he make supplication for his own sins?
₁ He himself, being flesh, nourishes wrath.₂ Who will make atonement for his sins?
₁ Remember your last end, and stop enmity.₂ Remember corruption and death, and be true to the commandments.
₁ Remember the commandments, and don’t be angry with your neighbour.₂ Remember the covenant of the Highest, and overlook ignorance.
₁ Abstain from strife, and you will diminish your sins,₂ for a passionate man will kindle strife.
₁ A man who is a sinner will trouble friends₂ and sow discord amongst those who are at peace.
₁ As is the fuel of the fire, so it will burn;₂ and as the stoutness of the strife is, so it will burn.₁ As is the strength of the man, so will be his wrath;₂ and as is his wealth, so he will exalt his anger.
₁ A contention begun in haste kindles a fire;₂ and hasty fighting sheds blood.
₁ If you blow on a spark, it will burn;₂ and if you spit upon it, it will be quenched.₂ Both of these come out of your mouth.
₁ Curse the whisperer and double-tongued,₂ for he has destroyed many who were at peace.

₁ A slanderer has threw out brave women₂ and deprived them of their labours.
₁ He who listens to it will not find rest,₂ nor will he live quietly.
₁ The stroke of a whip makes a mark in the flesh,₂ but the stroke of a tongue will break bones.
₁ Many have fallen by the edge of the sword,₂ yet not so many as those who have fallen because of the tongue.
₁ Happy is he who is sheltered from it,₂ who has not passed through its wrath,₂ who has not drawn its yoke,₂ and has not been bound with its bands.
₁ Because its yoke is a yoke of iron,₂ and its bands are bands of brass.

₁ Many have considered a loan to be a windfall,₂ and have given trouble to those who helped them.

₁ However be patient with a man in poor estate.₂ Don’t keep him waiting for your alms.

₁ A good man will be surety for his neighbour.₂ He who has lost shame will fail him.

₁ The essentials of life are water, bread,₂ a garment, and a house for privacy.

₁ All things are in pairs, one opposite the other.₂ He has made nothing imperfect.

₁ The pride of the heavenly heights is the clear sky,₂ the appearance of heaven, in the spectacle of its glory.
₁ The sun, when it appears, bringing tidings as it rises,₂ is a marvellous instrument, the work of the Most High.

₁ The moon marks the changing seasons,₂ declares times, and is a sign for the world.

₁ The month is called after its name,₂ increasing wonderfully in its changing—₂ an instrument of the army on high,₂ shining in the structure of heaven,

₁ At the word of the Holy One, they will stand in due order.₂ They won’t faint in their watches.
₁ Look at the rainbow, and praise him who made it.₂ It is exceedingly beautiful in its brightness.
₁ It encircles the sky with its glorious circle.₂ The hands of the Most High have stretched it out.
₁ By his commandment, he makes the snow fall₂ and swiftly sends the lightnings of his judgement.
₁ Therefore the storehouses are opened,₂ and clouds fly out like birds.
₁ By his mighty power, he makes the clouds strong₂ and the hailstones are broken in pieces.
₁ At his appearing, the mountains will be shaken.₂ At his will, the south wind will blow.
₁ The voice of his thunder rebukes the earth.₂ So does the northern storm and the whirlwind.₁ Like birds flying down, he sprinkles the snow.₂ It falls down like the lighting of locusts.

₁ He also pours out frost on the earth like salt.₂ When it is freezes, it has points like thorns.
₁ The cold north wind blows₂ and ice freezes on the water.₁ It settles on every pool of water.₂ The water puts it on like it was a breastplate.

₁ A mist coming speedily heals all things.₂ A dew coming after heat brings cheerfulness.
₁ By his counsel, he has calmed the deep₂ and planted islands in it.
₁ Those who sail on the sea tell of its dangers.₂ We marvel when we hear it with our ears.
₁ There are also those strange and wondrous works in it—₂ variety of all that has life and the huge creatures of the sea.
₁ Because of him, his messengers succeed.₂ By his word, all things hold together.
₁ We may say many things, but couldn’t say enough.₂ The summary of our words is, “He is everything!”
₁ How could we have strength to glorify him?₂ Because he is himself the greater than all his works.
₁ The master is awesome and exceedingly great!₂ His power is marvellous!
₁ Glorify the master and exalt him as much as you can!₂ Because even yet, he will surpass that.₁ When you exalt him, summon your full strength.₂ Don’t be weary, because you can’t praise him enough.
₁ Who has seen him, that he may describe him?₂ Who can magnify him as he is?
₁ Many things greater than these are hidden,₂ for we have seen just a few of his works.
₁ Because the master made all things.₂ He gave wisdom to the godly.
₁ Let us now praise famous men,₂ our ancestors in their generations.

₁ Abraham was a great father of a multitude of nations.₂ There was none found like him in glory,
₂ who kept the law of the Most High,₂ and was taken into covenant with him.₁ In his flesh he established the covenant.₂ When he was tested, he was found faithful.
₁ Therefore he assured him by an oath₂ that the nations would be blessed through his offspring,₂ that he would multiply him like the dust of the earth,₂ exalt his offspring like the stars,₂ and cause them to inherit from sea to sea,₂ and from the Euphrates River to the utmost parts of the earth.
₁ In Isaac also, he established the same assurance for Abraham his father’s sake,₂ the blessing of all men, and the covenant.
₁ He made it rest upon the head of Jacob.₂ He acknowledged him in his blessings,₂ gave to him by inheritance,₂ and divided his portions.₂ He distributed them amongst twelve tribes.
₁ He brought out of him a man of mercy,₂ who found favour in the sight of all people,₂ a man loved by God and men, even Moses,₂ whose memory is blessed.
₁ He made him equal to the glory of the saints,₂ and magnified him in the fears of his enemies.
₁ By his words he caused the wonders to cease.₂ God glorified him in the sight of kings.₁ He gave him commandments for his people₂ and showed him part of his glory.
₁ He sanctified him in his faithfulness and meekness.₂ He chose him out of all people.
₁ He made him to hear his voice,₂ led him into the thick darkness,₂ and gave him commandments face to face,₂ even the law of life and knowledge,₂ that he might teach Jacob the covenant,₂ and Israel his judgements.
₁ He exalted Aaron, a holy man like Moses,₂ even his brother, of the tribe of Levi.
₁ He established an everlasting covenant with him,₂ and gave him the priesthood of the people.₁ He blessed him with stateliness,₂ and dressed him in a glorious robe.
₁ He clothed him in perfect splendour,₂ and strengthened him with symbols of authority:₂ the linen trousers, the long robe, and the ephod.
₁ He encircled him with pomegranates;₂ with many golden bells around him,₂ to make a sound as he went,₂ to make a sound that might be heard in the temple,₂ for a reminder for the children of his people;
₂ with a holy garment, with gold, blue, and purple, the work of the embroiderer;₂ with an oracle of judgement—Urim and Thummim;
₂ with twisted scarlet, the work of the craftsman;₂ with precious stones engraved like a signet, in a setting of gold, the work of the jeweller,₂ for a reminder engraved in writing, after the number of the tribes of Israel;
₂ with a crown of gold upon the mitre, having engraved on it, as on a signet, “HOLINESS”,₂ an ornament of honour, the work of an expert,₂ the desires of the eyes, goodly and beautiful.
₁ Before him there never have been anything like it.₂ No stranger put them on, but only his sons and his offspring perpetually.
₁ His sacrifices shall be wholly burnt,₂ twice every day continually.
₁ Moses consecrated him,₂ and anointed him with holy oil.₁ It was an everlasting covenant with him₂ and to his offspring, all the days of heaven,₂ to minister to the master, to serve as a priest,₂ and to bless his people in his name.
₁ He chose him out of all living₂ to offer sacrifice to the master—₂ incense, and a sweet fragrance, for a memorial,₂ to make atonement for your people.
₁ He gave to him in his commandments,₂ authority in the covenants of judgements,₂ to teach Jacob the testimonies,₂ and to enlighten Israel in his law.
₁ Strangers conspired against him₂ and envied him in the wilderness:₂ Dathan and Abiram with their company,₂ and the congregation of Korah, with wrath and anger.
₁ The master saw it, and it displeased him.₂ In the wrath of his anger, they were destroyed.₁ He did wonders upon them,₂ to consume them with flaming fire.
₁ He added glory to Aaron,₂ and gave him a heritage.₁ He divided to him the first fruits of the increase,₂ and prepared bread of first fruits in abundance.
₁ Because they eat the sacrifices of the master,₂ which he gave to him and to his offspring.
₁ However, in the land of the people, he has no inheritance,₂ and he has no portion amongst the people,₂ for the master himself is your portion and inheritance.
₁ Phinehas the son of Eleazar is the third in glory,₂ in that he was zealous in the fear of the master,₂ and stood fast when the people turned away,₂ and he made atonement for Israel.
₁ Therefore, a covenant of peace was established for him,₂ that he should be leader of the sanctuary and of his people,₂ that he and his offspring should have the dignity of the priesthood forever.
₁ Also he made a covenant with David the son of Yishay \add (Jesse)\add*, of the tribe of Yehudah \add (Judah)\add*.₂ The inheritance of the king is his alone from son to son.₂ So the inheritance of Aaron is also to his seed.
₁ May God give you wisdom in your heart₂ to judge his people in righteousness,₂ that their good things may not be abolished,₂ and that their glory may endure for all their generations.
₁ Joshua the son of Nun was valiant in war,₂ and was the successor of Moses in prophecies.₁ He was made great according to his name₂ for the saving of\f + \fr 46:1 \ft Gr. \fqa his.\f* God’s elect,₂ to take vengeance on the enemies that rose up against them,₂ that he might give Israel their inheritance.
₁ How was he glorified in the lifting up his hands,₂ and in stretching out his sword against the cities!
₁ Who before him stood so firm?₂ Because the master himself brought his enemies to him.
₁ Didn’t the sun go back by his hand?₂ Didn’t one day become as two?
₁ He called upon the Most High, the Mighty One,₂ when his foes pressed in all around him,₂ and the great master heard him.

₁ Also the judges, every one by his name,₂ all whose hearts didn’t engage in immorality,₂ and who didn’t turn away from the master—₂ may their memory be blessed!
₁ May their bones flourish again out of their place.₂ May the name of those who have been honoured be renewed in their children.
₁ Samuel, the prophet of the master, loved by his master,₂ established a kingdom and anointed princes over his people.
₁ By the law of the master he judged the congregation,₂ and the master watched over Jacob.
₁ By his faithfulness he was proved to be a prophet.₂ By his words he was known to be faithful in vision.
₁ When his enemies pressed on him on every side,₂ he called upon the master, the Mighty One,₂ with the offering of the suckling lamb.
₁ Then the master thundered from heaven.₂ He made his voice heard with a mighty sound.
₁ He utterly destroyed the rulers of the Tyrians₂ and all the princes of the Philistines.
₁ Before the time of his age-long sleep,₂ he testified in the sight of the lord and his anointed,₂ “I have not taken any man’s goods, so much as a sandal;”₂ and no one accused him.
₁ Even after he fell asleep, he prophesied,₂ and showed the king his end,₂ and lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy,₂ to blot out the wickedness of the people.
₁ After him, Nathan rose up₂ to prophesy in the days of David.
₁ As is the fat when it is separated from the peace offering,₂ so was David separated from the children of Israel.
₁ He played with lions as with kids,₂ and with bears as with lambs of the flock.
₁ In his youth didn’t he kill a giant,₂ and take away reproach from the people₂ when he lifted up his hand with a sling stone,₂ and beat down the boasting Goliath?
₁ Because he called upon the Most High master,₂ and he gave him strength in his right hand₂ to kill a man mighty in war,₂ to exalt the horn of his people.
₁ So they glorified him for his tens of thousands,₂ and praised him for the blessings of the master,₂ in that a glorious diadem was given to him.
₁ Because he destroyed the enemies on every side,₂ and defeated the Philistines his adversaries.₂ He broke their horn in pieces to this day.
₁ In every work of his he gave thanks to the Holy One Most High with words of glory.₂ He sang praise with his whole heart,₂ and loved him who made him.

₁ He gave beauty to the feasts,₂ and set in order the seasons to completion₂ while they praised his holy name,₂ and the sanctuary resounded from early morning.
₁ The master took away his sins,₂ and exalted his horn forever.₁ He gave him a covenant of kings,₂ and a glorious throne in Israel.
₁ After him a wise son rose up,₂ who because of him lived in security.
₁ Solomon reigned in days of peace.₂ God gave him rest all around,₂ that he might set up a house for his name,₂ and prepare a sanctuary forever.
₁ How wise you were made in your youth,₂ and filled as a river with understanding!
₁ Your influence covered the earth,₂ and you filled it with parables and riddles.
₁ Your name reached to the far away islands,₂ and you were loved for your peace.
₁ Because your songs, proverbs, parables,₂ and interpretations, the countries marvelled at you.
₁ By the name of the master God,₂ who is called the god of Israel,₂ you gathered gold like tin,₂ and multiplied silver like lead.
₁ You bowed your loins to women,₂ and in your body you were brought into subjection.
₁ You blemished your honour,₂ and defiled your offspring,₂ to bring wrath upon your children.₂ I was grieved for your folly,
₂ because the sovereignty was divided,₂ and a disobedient kingdom ruled out of Ephraim.
₁ But the master will never forsake his mercy.₂ He won’t destroy any of his works,₂ nor blot out the posterity of his elect.₁ He won’t take away the offspring him who loved him.₂ He gave a remnant to Jacob,₂ and to David a root from his own family.
₁ So Solomon rested with his fathers.₂ Of his offspring, he left behind him Rehoboam,₂ the foolishness of the people, and one who lacked understanding,₂ who made the people revolt by his counsel.₁ Also Jeroboam the son of Nebat,₂ who made Israel to sin,₂ and gave a way of sin to Ephraim.
₁ Their sins were multiplied exceedingly,₂ until they were removed from their land.
₁ Because they sought out all manner of wickedness,₂ until vengeance came upon them.

₁ He brought a famine upon them,₂ and by his zeal made them few in number.

¶ These are the words of the book which Baruch the son of Nerias, the son of Maaseas, the son of Sedekias, the son of Asadias, the son of Helkias, wrote in Babylon,
in the fifth year, in the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans took Jerusalem and burnt it with fire.
Baruch read the words of this book in the hearing of Jechonias the son of Joakim king of Judah, and in the hearing of all the people who came to hear the book,
and in the hearing of the mighty men, and of the kings’ sons, and in the hearing of the elders, and in the hearing of all the people, from the least to the greatest, even of all those who lived at Babylon by the river Sud.
Then they wept, fasted,\f + \fr 1:5 \ft Another reading is, \fqa and vowed vows.\f* and prayed before the master.
They also made a collection of money according to every man’s ability;
and they sent it to Jerusalem to Joakim the high priest, the son of Helkias, the son of Salom, and to the priests and to all the people who were found with him at Jerusalem,
at the same time when he took the vessels of the house of the master, that had been carried out of the temple, to return them into the land of Judah, the tenth day of Sivan—silver vessels which Sedekias the son of Josias king of Judah had made,
after Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon had carried away Jechonias, the princes, the captives, the mighty men, and the people of the land from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon.
¶ And they said: Listen, we have sent you money; therefore buy with the money burnt offerings, sin offerings, and incense, and prepare an oblation, and offer upon the altar of the master our god;
and pray for the life of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and for the life of Baltasar his son, that their days may be\f + \fr 1:11 \ft See Deuteronomy 11:21.\f* as the days of heaven above the earth.
The master will give us strength and light to our eyes. We will live under the shadow of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon and under the shadow of Baltasar his son, and we shall serve them many days, and find favour in their sight.
Pray for us also to the master our god, for we have sinned against the master our god. To this day the wrath of the master and his indignation is not turned from us.
You shall read this book which we have sent to you, to make confession in the house of the master upon the day of the feast and on the days of the solemn assembly.
¶ You shall say: To the master our god belongs righteousness, but to us confusion of face, as at this day—to the men of Judah, to the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
to our kings, to our princes, to our priests, to our prophets, and to our fathers,
because we have sinned before the master.
We have disobeyed him and have not listened to the voice of the master our god, to walk in the commandments of the master that he has set before us.
Since the day that the master brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt to this present day, we have been disobedient to the master our god, and we have been negligent in not listening to his voice.
Therefore the plagues have clung to us, along with the curse which the master declared through Moses his servant in the day that he brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt to give us a land that flows with milk and honey, as at this day.
Nevertheless we didn’t listen to the voice of the master our god, according to all the words of the prophets whom he sent to us,
but we each walked in the imagination of his own wicked heart, to serve strange gods and to do what is evil in the sight of the master our god.
¶ Therefore the master has made good his word which he pronounced against us, and against our judges who judged Israel, and against our kings, and against our princes, and against the men of Israel and Judah,
to bring upon us great plagues such as never happened before under the whole heaven,\f + \fr 2:2 \ft Another reading is, \fqa even as he has done.\f* as it came to pass in Jerusalem, according to the things that are written in the law of Moses,
that we should each eat the flesh of our own son, and each eat the flesh of our own daughter.
Moreover he has given them to be in subjection to all the kingdoms that are around us, to be a reproach and a desolation amongst all the people around us, where the master has scattered them.
Thus they were threw down and not exalted, because we sinned against the master our god in not listening to his voice.
To the master our god belongs righteousness, but to us and to our fathers confusion of face, as at this day.
All these plagues have come upon us which the master has pronounced against us.
Yet have we not entreated the favour of the master by everyone turning from the thoughts of his wicked heart.
Therefore the master has kept watch over the plagues. The master has brought them upon us, for the master is righteous in all his works which he has commanded us.
Yet we have not listened to his voice, to walk in the commandments of the master that he has set before us.
¶ And now, O master, you God of Israel who have brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, with signs, with wonders, with great power, and with a high arm, and have gotten yourself a name, as at this day:
O master our god, we have sinned. We have been ungodly. We have done wrong in all your ordinances.
Let your wrath turn from us, for we are but a few left amongst the heathen where you have scattered us.
Hear our prayer, O master, and our petition, and deliver us for your own sake. Give us favour in the sight of those who have led us away captive,
that all the earth may know that you are the master our god, because Israel and his posterity is called by your name.
O master, look down from your holy house and consider us. Incline your ear, O master, and hear.
Open your eyes, and see; for the dead that are in Hades, whose breath is taken from their bodies, will give to the master neither glory nor righteousness;
but the soul who is greatly vexed, who goes stooping and feeble, and the eyes that fail, and the hungry soul, will declare your glory and righteousness, O master.
¶ Because we do not present our supplication before you, O master our god, for the righteousness of our fathers and of our kings.
Because you have sent your wrath and your indignation upon us, as you have spoken by your servants the prophets, saying,
“The master says, ‘Bow your shoulders to serve the king of Babylon, and remain in the land that I gave to your fathers.
But if you won’t hear the voice of the master to serve the king of Babylon,
I will cause to cease out of the cities of Judah and from the region near Jerusalem the voice of mirth, the voice of gladness, voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride. The whole land will be desolate without inhabitant.’ ”
But we wouldn’t listen to your voice, to serve the king of Babylon. Therefore you have made good your words that you spoke by your servants the prophets, that the bones of our kings and the bones of our fathers would be taken out of their places.
Listen, they are threw out to the heat by day and to the frost by night. They died in great miseries by famine, by sword, and by\f + \fr 2:25 \ft See Jeremiah 32:36.\f* pestilence.
You have made the house that is called by your name as it is today because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
¶ Yet, O master our god, you have dealt with us after all your kindness and according to all your great mercy,
as you spoke by your servant Moses in the day when you commanded him to write your law in the presence of the children of Israel, saying,
“If you won’t hear my voice, surely this very great multitude will be turned into a small number amongst the nations where I will scatter them.
Because I know that they will not hear me, because they are a stiff-necked people; but in the land of their captivity they will take it to heart,
and will know that I am the master their god. I will give them a heart and ears to hear.
Then they will praise me in the land of their captivity, and think about my name,
and will return from their stiff neck and from their wicked deeds; for they will remember the way of their fathers who sinned before the master.
I will bring them again into the land which I promised to their fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, and they will rule over it. I will increase them, and they won’t be diminished.
And I will make an everlasting covenant with them to be their god, and they will be my people. I will no more remove my people Israel out of the land that I have given them.”
¶ O master Almighty, you God of Israel, the soul in anguish and the troubled spirit cries to you.
Hear, O master, and have mercy; for you are a merciful God. Yes, have mercy upon us, because we have sinned before you.
Because you are enthroned forever, and we keep perishing.
O master Almighty, you God of Israel, hear now the prayer of the dead Israelites, and of the children of those who were sinners before you, who didn’t listen to the voice of you their god; because of this, these plagues cling to us.
Don’t remember the iniquities of our fathers, but remember your power and your name at this time.
Because you are the master our god, and we will praise you, O master.
Because this cause, you have put your fear in our hearts, to the intent that we should call upon your name. We will praise you in our captivity, for we have called to mind all the iniquity of our fathers who sinned before you.
Listen, we are yet this day in our captivity where you have scattered us, for a reproach and a curse, and to be subject to penalty according to all the iniquities of our fathers who departed from the master our god.
¶ Hear, O Israel, the commandments of life! Give ear to understand wisdom!
How is it, O Israel, that you are in your enemies’ land, that you have become old in a strange country, that you are defiled with the dead,
that you are counted with those who are in Hades?
You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom.
If you had walked in the way of God, you would have dwelled in peace forever.
Learn where there is wisdom, where there is strength, and where there is understanding, that you may also know where there is length of days and life, where there is the light of the eyes and peace.
Who has found out her place? Who has come into her treasuries?
Where are the princes of the heathen, and those who ruled the \add wild\add* animals that are on the earth,
those who had their pastime with the fowls of the air, and those who hoarded up silver and gold, in which people trust, and of their getting there is no end?
Because those who diligently sought silver, and were so anxious, and whose works are past finding out,
they have vanished and gone down to Hades, and others have come up in their place.
¶ Younger men have seen the light and lived upon the earth, but they haven’t known the way of knowledge,
nor understood its paths. Their children haven’t embraced it. They are far off from their way.
It has not been heard of in Canaan, neither has it been seen in Teman.
The sons also of Agar who seek understanding, which are in the land, the merchants of Merran and Teman, and the authors of fables, and the searchers out of understanding—none of these have known the way of wisdom or remembered her paths.
¶ O Israel, how great is the house of God! How large is the place of his possession!
It is great and has no end. It is high and unmeasurable.
Giants were born that were famous of old, great of stature, and expert in war.
God didn’t choose these, nor did he give the way of knowledge to them,
so they perished, because they had no wisdom. They perished through their own foolishness.
Who has gone up into heaven, taken her, and brought her down from the clouds?
Who has gone over the sea, found her, and will bring her for choice gold?
There is no one who knows her way, nor any who comprehend her path.
But he that knows all things knows her, he found her out with his understanding. He who prepared the earth for all time has filled it with four-footed animals.
It is he who sends forth the light, and it goes. He called it, and it obeyed him with fear.
The stars shone in their watches, and were glad. When he called them, they said, “Here we are.” They shone with gladness to him who made them.
This is our god. No other can be compared to him.
He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant and to Israel who is loved by him.
Afterward she appeared upon earth, and lived with men.

¶ This is the book of God’s commandments and the law that endures forever. All those who hold it fast will live, but those who leave it will die.
Turn, O Jacob, and take hold of it. Walk towards the shining of its light.
Don’t give your glory to another, nor the things that are to your advantage to a foreign nation.
O Israel, we are happy; for the things that are pleasing to God are made known to us.
¶ Be of good cheer, my people, the memorial of Israel.
You were not sold to the nations for destruction, but because you moved God to wrath, you were delivered to your adversaries.
Because you provoked him who made you by sacrificing to demons and not to God.
You forgot the everlasting God who brought you up. You also grieved Jerusalem, who nursed you.
Because she saw the wrath that came upon you from God, and said, “Listen, you who dwell near Tsiyyon \add (Zion)\add*; for God has brought upon me great mourning.
Because I have seen the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting has brought upon them.
Because with joy I nourished them, but sent them away with weeping and mourning.
Let no man rejoice over me, a widow and forsaken by many. Because the sins of my children, I am left desolate, because they turned away from the law of God
and had no regard for his statutes. They didn’t walk in the ways of God’s commandments or tread in the paths of discipline in his righteousness.
Let those who dwell near Tsiyyon \add (Zion)\add* come and remember the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting has brought upon them.
Because he has brought a nation upon them from afar, a shameless nation with a strange language, who didn’t respect old men or pity children.
They have carried away the dear beloved sons of the widow, and left her who was alone desolate of her daughters.”
¶ But I—how can I help you?
Because he who brought these calamities upon you will deliver you from the hand of your enemies.
Go your way, O my children. Go your way, for I am left desolate.
I have put off the garment of peace, and put on the sackcloth of my petition. I will cry to the Everlasting as long as I live.
¶ Take courage, my children. Cry to God, and he will deliver you from the power and hand of the enemies.
Because I have trusted in the Everlasting, that he will save you; and joy has come to me from the Holy One, because of the mercy that will soon come to you from your Everlasting Saviour.
Because I sent you out with mourning and weeping, but God will give you to me again with joy and gladness forever.
Because as now those who dwell near Tsiyyon \add (Zion)\add* have seen your captivity, so they will shortly see your salvation from our god which will come upon you with great glory and brightness of the Everlasting.
My children, suffer patiently the wrath that has come upon you from God, for your enemy has persecuted you; but shortly you will see his destruction and will tread upon their necks.
My delicate ones have travelled rough roads. They were taken away like a flock carried off by enemies.
¶ Take courage, my children, and cry to God; for you will be remembered by him who has brought this upon you.
Because as it was your decision to go astray from God, return and seek him ten times more.
Because he who brought these calamities upon you will bring you everlasting joy again with your salvation.
Take courage, O Jerusalem, for he who called you by name will comfort you.
Miserable are those who afflicted you and rejoiced at your fall.
Miserable are the cities which your children served. Miserable is she who received your sons.
Because as she rejoiced at your fall and was glad of your ruin, so she will be grieved at her own desolation.
And I will take away her pride in her great multitude and her boasting will be turned into mourning.
Because fire will come upon her from the Everlasting for many days; and she will be inhabited by demons for a long time.
¶ O Jerusalem, look around you towards the east, and behold the joy that comes to you from God.
Listen, your sons come, whom you sent away. They come gathered together from the east to the west at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.
¶ Take off the garment of your mourning and affliction, O Jerusalem, and put on forever the beauty of the glory from God.
Put on the robe of the righteousness from God. Set on your head a diadem of the glory of the Everlasting.
Because God will show your splendour everywhere under heaven.
Because your name will be called by God forever “Righteous Peace, Godly Glory”.
¶ Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand upon the height. Look around you towards the east and see your children gathered from the going down of the sun to its rising at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing that God has remembered them.
Because they went from you on foot, being led away by their enemies, but God brings them in to you carried on high with glory, on a royal throne.
Because God has appointed that every high mountain and the everlasting hills should be made low, and the valleys filled up to make the ground level, that Israel may go safely in the glory of God.
Moreover the woods and every sweet smelling tree have shaded Israel by the commandment of God.
Because God will lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that come from him.





















































































































































































































































¶ After Alexander the Macedonian, the son of Philip, who came out of the land of Chittim, and struck Darius king of the Persians and Medes, it came to pass, after he had struck him, that he reigned in his place, in former time, over\f + \fr 1:1 \ft That is, the Greek Empire. Compare 1 Maccabees 1:10 and 1 Maccabees 6:2.\f* Greece.
He fought many battles, won many strongholds, killed the kings of the earth,
went through to the ends of the earth, and took spoils of a multitude of nations. The earth was quiet before him. He was exalted. His heart was lifted up.
He gathered together an exceedingly strong army and ruled over countries, nations, and principalities, and they paid him tribute.
¶ After these things he fell sick, and perceived that he was going to die.
He called his honourable servants, which had been brought up with him from his youth, and he divided to them his kingdom while he was still alive.
Alexander reigned twelve years, then he died.
Then his servants ruled, each one in his place.
They all put crowns upon themselves after he was dead, and so did their sons after them many years; and they multiplied evils in the earth.
¶ There came out of them a sinful root, Antiochus Epiphanes, son of Antiochus the king, who had been a hostage at Rome, and he reigned in\f + \fr 1:10 \ft circa B.C. 176.\f* the one hundred and thirty seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks.
¶ In those days transgressors of the law came out of Israel and persuaded many, saying, “Let’s go make a covenant with the\f + \fr 1:11 \ft Or, \fqa nations: \ft and so throughout this book.\f* Gentiles around us; for since we were separated from them many evils have befallen us.”
That proposal was good in their eyes.
Some of the people eagerly went to the king, and he authorised them to observe the ordinances of the\f + \fr 1:13 \ft Or, \fqa nations: \ft and so throughout this book.\f* Gentiles.
So\f + \fr 1:14 \ft See 2 Maccabees 4:9, 12.\f* they built a gymnasium in Jerusalem according to the laws of the\f + \fr 1:14 \ft Or, \fqa nations: \ft and so throughout this book.\f* Gentiles.
They made themselves uncircumcised, forsook the holy covenant, joined themselves to the\f + \fr 1:15 \ft Or, \fqa nations: \ft and so throughout this book\f* Gentiles, and sold themselves to do evil.
¶ The kingdom was established in the sight of Antiochus, and he planned to reign over Egypt, that he might reign over both kingdoms.
He entered into Egypt with a\f + \fr 1:17 \ft Gr. \fqa heavy.\f* great multitude, with chariots, with elephants, with cavalry, and with a great\f + \fr 1:17 \ft Or, \fqa armament\f* navy.
He made war against Ptolemy king of Egypt. Ptolemy was put to shame before him, and fled; and many fell wounded to death.
They took possession of the strong cities in the land of Egypt, and he took the spoils of Egypt.
¶ Antiochus, after he had defeated Egypt, returned in\f + \fr 1:20 \ft circa B.C. 170. See 2 Maccabees 5:11-16.\f* the one hundred and forty third year, and went up against Israel and Jerusalem with a\f + \fr 1:20 \ft Gr. \fqa heavy.\f* great multitude,
and entered presumptuously into the sanctuary, and took the golden altar, the lampstand for the light, and all its utensils.
He took the table of the show bread, the cups for the drink offerings, the bowls, the golden censers, the veil, the crowns, and the gold decoration on the front of the temple. He peeled it all off.
He took the silver, the gold, and the precious vessels. He took the hidden treasures which he found.
When he had taken all of these, he went away into his own land. He made a great slaughter, and spoke very arrogantly.
Great mourning came upon Israel, in every place where they were.
The rulers and elders groaned. The virgins and young men were made feeble. The beauty of the women was changed.
Every bridegroom took up lamentation. She who sat in the marriage chamber was mourning.
The land was moved for its inhabitants, and all the house of Jacob was clothed with shame.
¶ \f + \fr 1:29 \ft See 2 Maccabees 5:24.\f*After two full years, the king sent a chief collector of tribute to the cities of Judah, and he came to Jerusalem with a\f + \fr 1:29 \ft Gr. \fqa heavy.\f* great multitude.
He spoke words of peace to them in subtlety, and they believed him. Then he fell upon the city suddenly, struck it very severely, and destroyed many people of Israel.
He took the spoils of the city, set it on fire, and pulled down its houses and its walls on every side.
They led captive the women and the children, and seized the livestock.
Then they fortified the city of David with a large, strong wall and with strong towers, and it became their citadel.
They put a sinful nation, transgressors of the law, there, and they strengthened themselves in it.
They stored up weapons and food, and gathering together the spoils of Jerusalem, they stored them there, and they became a great menace.
It became a place to lie in wait against the sanctuary, and an evil adversary to Israel continually.
They shed innocent blood on every side of the sanctuary, and defiled the sanctuary.
The inhabitants of Jerusalem fled because of them. She became a habitation of foreigners. She became foreign to those who were born in her, and her children forsook her.
Her sanctuary was laid waste like a wilderness,\f + \fr 1:39 \ft See 2 Maccabees 6:6.\f* her feasts were turned into mourning, her Sabbaths into reproach, and her honour into contempt.
According to her glory, so was her dishonour multiplied, and her exaltation was turned into mourning.
¶ King Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom that all should be one people,
and that each should forsake his own laws. All the nations agreed according to the word of the king.
Many of Israel consented to his worship, sacrificed to the idols, and profaned the Sabbath.
The king sent letters by the hand of messengers to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, that they should follow laws strange to the land,
and should forbid whole burnt offerings and sacrifice and drink offerings in the sanctuary; and should profane the Sabbaths and feasts,
and pollute the sanctuary and those who were holy;
that they should build altars, and temples, and shrines for idols, and should sacrifice swine’s flesh and unclean animals;
and that they should leave their sons uncircumcised, that they should make their souls abominable with all manner of uncleanness and profanation;
so that they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.
Whoever doesn’t do according to the word of the king, he shall die.
According to all these words wrote he to his whole kingdom. He appointed overseers over all the people, and he commanded the cities of Judah to sacrifice, city by city.
From the people were gathered together to them many, everyone who had forsaken the law; and they did evil things in the land.
They made Israel to hide themselves in every place of refuge which they had.
¶ On the fifteenth day of Chislev, in\f + \fr 1:54 \ft circa B.C. 168. See 2 Maccabees 5:11.\f* the one hundred and forty fifth year, they built an abomination of desolation upon the altar,\f + \fr 1:54 \ft The two words rendered \fqa altar \ft are different in the Greek: and so in 1 Maccabees 1:59.\f* and in the cities of Judah on every side they built idol altars.\f + \fr 1:54 \ft The two words rendered \fqa altar \ft are different in the Greek: and so in 1 Maccabees 1:59.\f*
At the doors of the houses and in the streets they burnt incense.
They tore the books of the law which they found in pieces and set them on fire.
Anyone who was found with any a book of the covenant, and if any consented to the law, the king’s sentence delivered him to death.
Thus did they in their might to Israel, to those who were found month by month in the cities.
On the twenty-fifth day of the month they sacrificed upon the idol altar that was on top of the altar of burnt offering.
\f + \fr 1:60 \ft See 2 Maccabees 6:10.\f*They put to death women who had circumcised their children, according to the commandment.
They hung their babies around their necks, and their houses, and those who had circumcised them.
Many in Israel were fully resolved and confirmed in themselves not to eat unclean things.
\f + \fr 1:63 \ft See 2 Maccabees 6:19 and 7:1, etc.\f*They chose to die, that they might not be defiled with the food, and that they might not profane the holy covenant; and they died.
Exceedingly great wrath came upon Israel.
¶ In those days Mattathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, from Jerusalem rose up; and he lived at Modin.
And he had five sons:\f + \fr 2:2 \ft Gr. \fqa Joannes.\f* John, who was surnamed Gaddis;
Simon, who was called Thassi;
Judas, who was called Maccabaeus;
Eleazar, who was called Avaran; and Jonathan, who was called Apphus.
¶ He saw the blasphemies that were committed in Judah and in Jerusalem,
and he said, “Woe is me! Why was I born to see the destruction of my people and the destruction of the holy city, and to dwell there when it was given into the hand of the enemy, the sanctuary into the hand of foreigners?
Her temple has become like a man who was glorious.
Her vessels of glory are carried away into captivity. Her infants are slain in her streets. Her young men are slain with the enemy’s sword.
What nation has not inherited her palaces and taken possession of her spoils?
Her adornment has all been taken away. Instead of a free woman, she has become a slave.
Listen, our holy things, our beauty, and our glory are laid waste. The Gentiles have profaned them.
Why should we live any longer?”
¶ Mattathias and his sons tore their clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourned exceedingly.
¶ And the king’s officers who were enforcing the apostasy came into the city Modin to sacrifice.
Many of Israel came to them, and Mattathias and his sons were gathered together.
The king’s officers answered and spoke to Mattathias, saying, “You are a ruler and an honourable and great man in this city, and strengthened with sons and kindred.
Now therefore come first and do the commandment of the king, as all the nations have done, including the men of Judah and those who remain in Jerusalem. You and your house will be numbered amongst the king’s\f + \fr 2:18 \ft See 1 Maccabees 3:38; 10:10, etc.; Compare 1 Maccabees 10:65; 11:27; 2 Maccabees 8:9.\f* friends, and you and your sons will be honoured with silver and gold and many gifts.”
¶ And Mattathias answered and said with a loud voice, “If all the nations that are in the house of the king’s dominion listen to him, to fall away each one from the worship of his fathers, and have made choice to follow his commandments,
yet I and my sons and my kindred will walk in the covenant of our fathers.
Far be it from us that we should forsake the law and the ordinances.
We will not listen to the king’s words, to turn aside from our worship, to the right hand, or to the left.”
¶ When he had finished speaking these words, a Jew came in the sight of all to sacrifice on the altar which was at Modin, according to the king’s commandment.
Mattathias saw it, so his zeal was kindled, and his guts trembled, and he vented his wrath according to judgement, and ran and killed him upon the altar.
He killed the king’s officer, who compelled men to sacrifice, at the same time, and pulled down the altar.
He was zealous for the law, even as Phinehas did to Zimri the son of Salu.
¶ Mattathias cried out in the city with a loud voice, saying, “Whoever is zealous for the law and maintains the covenant, let him follow me!”
He and his sons fled into the mountains, and left all that they had in the city.
¶ Then many who sought justice and judgement went down into the wilderness to live there—
they, their children, their wives, and their livestock—because evils were multiplied upon them.
It was told the king’s officers and the forces that were in Jerusalem, the city of David, that certain men who had broken the king’s commandment had gone down into the secret places in the wilderness;
and many pursued after them, and having overtaken them, they encamped against them and set the battle in array against them on the Sabbath day.
They said to them, “Enough of this! Come out and do according to the word of the king, and you will all live!”
¶ They said, “We won’t come out. We won’t do the word of the king, to profane the Sabbath day.”
¶ Then the enemy hurried to attack them.
¶ They didn’t answer them. They didn’t threw a stone at them, or block their secret places,
saying, “Let’s all die in our innocence. Heaven and earth testify for us, that you put us to death unjustly.”
¶ So they attacked them on the Sabbath, and they died—they, their wives, their children, and their livestock—in number a thousand souls of men.
¶ When Mattathias and his friends found out about it, and they mourned over them exceedingly.
One said to another, “If we all do as our kindred have done, and don’t fight against the Gentiles for our lives and our ordinances, they will quickly destroy us from off the earth.”
So they decided that day, saying, “Whoever comes against us to battle on the Sabbath day, let’s fight against him, and we will in no way all die, as our kindred died in the secret places.”
¶ Then a company of the Hasidaeans,\f + \fr 2:42 \ft That is, \fqa Chasidim.\f* mighty men of Israel, everyone who offered himself willingly for the law, were gathered together to them.
All those who fled from the evils were added to them, and supported them.
They mustered an army, and struck sinners in their anger, and lawless men in their wrath. The rest fled to the Gentiles for safety.
And Mattathias and his friends went around and pulled down the altars.
They forcibly circumcised the boys who were uncircumcised, as many as they found in the coasts of Israel.
They pursued the arrogant, and the work prospered in their hand.
They rescued the law out of the hand of the Gentiles and out of the hand of the kings. They never allowed the sinner to triumph.
¶ The days of Mattathias drew near that he should die, and he said to his sons, “Now pride and scorn have gained strength. It is a season of overthrow and indignant wrath.
Now, my children, be zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.
Call to remembrance the deeds of our fathers which they did in their generations; and receive great glory and an everlasting name.
Wasn’t Abraham found faithful in temptation, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness?
Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment, and became lord of Egypt.
Phinehas our father, because he was exceedingly zealous, obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
Joshua became a judge in Israel for fulfilling the word.
Caleb obtained a heritage in the land for testifying in the congregation.
David inherited the throne of a kingdom forever and ever for being merciful.
Elijah was taken up into heaven because he was exceedingly zealous for the law.
Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael believed, and were saved out of the flame.
Daniel was delivered from the mouth of lions for his innocence.
¶ “Thus consider from generation to generation that no one who put their trust in him will lack for strength.
Don’t be afraid of the words of a sinful man; for his glory will be dung and worms.
Today he will be lifted up, and tomorrow he will in no way be found, because he has returned to dust, and his thought has perished.
You, my children, be strong, and show yourselves men on behalf of the law; for in it you will obtain glory.
Listen, Simon your brother, whom I know to be a man of counsel. Always listen to him. He shall be a father to you.
Judas Maccabaeus has been strong and mighty from his youth. He shall be your captain and shall fight\f + \fr 2:66 \ft Some ancient authorities read \fqa you shall fight.\f* the battle of the people.
Rally around all the doers of the law, and avenge the wrong done to your people.
Repay the Gentiles, and obey the commandments of the law.”
¶ He blessed them, and was gathered to his ancestors.
He died in\f + \fr 2:70 \ft circa B.C. 167.\f* the one hundred and forty sixth year, and his sons buried him in the tombs of his ancestors at Modin. All Israel made great lamentation for him.
¶ His son Judas, who was called Maccabaeus, rose up in his place.
All his kindred helped him, and so did all those who joined with his father, and they fought with gladness the battle of Israel.
He got his people great glory, and put on a breastplate like a giant, and bound his warlike harness around him, and set battles in array, protecting the army with his sword.
He was like a lion in his deeds, and like a lion’s cub roaring for prey.
He hunted and pursued the lawless, and he burnt up those who troubled his people.
The lawless shrunk back for fear of him, and all the workers of lawlessness were very troubled, and deliverance prospered in his hand.
He angered many kings and made Jacob glad with his acts. His memory is blessed forever.
He went through the cities of Judah, destroyed the ungodly\f + \fr 3:8 \ft Gr. \fqa out of it.\f* out of the land, and turned away wrath from Israel.
He was renowned to the utmost part of the earth. He gathered together those who were ready to perish.
¶ Apollonius gathered the Gentiles together with a great army from Shomron \add (Samaria)\add* to fight against Israel.
Judas learnt of it, and he went out to meet him, struck him, and killed him. Many fell wounded to death, and the rest fled.
They took their spoils, and Judas took Apollonius’ sword, and he fought with it all his days.
¶ Seron, the commander of the army of Syria, heard that Judas had gathered a large company, including a body of faithful men who stayed with him, went out to war.
He said, “I will make myself a name and get myself glory in the kingdom. I will fight against Judas and those who are with him, who despise the king’s command.
A mighty army of the ungodly went up with him to help him, to take vengeance on the children of Israel.
¶ He came near to the ascent of Beyt-Horon, and Judas went out to meet him with a small company.
But when they saw the army coming to meet them, they said to Judas, “What? Shall we be able, being a small company, to fight against so great and strong a multitude? We for our part are faint, having tasted no food this day.”
